note: Physics I.2, 185a12-14: natural things, all or some, are in motion, which is clear by induction (δῆλον δʼ ἐκ τῆς ἐπαγωγῆς), the counterpart of the prima via's sensu constat. Aristotle's kinēsis is physical change, one kind of the reduction from potency to act that the premise means (DISAMB-MOTION), so the passage bears on the premise in its physical-change instance. It is laid down as a starting point of natural science (ὑποκείσθω), not proved, and the bound Lean reading (SomeNaturalThingsAreInMotionReading) is an opaque Prop, so no formal step connects them.
